summary: The blueprint covers the major healthy human pancreas landscape, but targeted refinements are needed for stromal gating and rare endocrine specificity.

issues.description: The mesenchymal gate is heavily fibroblast/ECM-weighted, which is plausible for stellate/fibroblast cells but weak as a shared gate for pericytes and vascular smooth muscle.
issues.suggested_fix: Broaden the stromal/mural gating design by adding mural markers to an inclusive mesenchymal/mural core, or make the mural identity a plain or less fibroblast-gated axis while retaining fibroblast/stellate resolution separately.

issues.description: The epsilon-cell module is driven by one specific marker, GHRL, plus several generic endocrine markers, so it may not separate epsilon cells robustly from other endocrine cells.
issues.suggested_fix: Strengthen the module with additional literature-supported human epsilon/ghrelin-cell markers if available, or reduce generic endocrine overlap so the axis is mainly driven by epsilon-specific signal.

issues.description: The activated stellate/myofibroblast program is recognizable but leans toward injury/fibrosis or dissociation-activated remodeling in an otherwise healthy baseline pancreas scenario.
issues.suggested_fix: Reframe or rename this as a stromal matrix-remodeling/activation state gated within stellate/fibroblast biology, rather than presenting it as a separate healthy lineage on par with quiescent fibroblast/stellate or mural cells.

out_of_scope: Citation verification was not performed; this review only judged biological coverage and marker plausibility.
